title: This Insurmountable Evil That Hangs Above Us All

lines.text: The sky is an iron dome
My breath curls and freezes amid the air
Above us, a mass too heavy to weigh
That presses the marrow from our bones
Daylight fractures into rusted shards
A blackened disc devours the horizon
Its ragged corona shuddering like torn wings
The wind carries dust that tastes of graves
And every heartbeat sounds like earth cracking
Invisible cables descend cold, glistening strands
That tangle the clouds, tugging at the oceans, the blood, the will
We stare upward, eyelids aflame
Unable to blink away the omen
No prophet speaks
Only an iron silence
Ringing as though a cathedral bell were tolling
Inside the skull
Hanging above all names
Above all prayers
A power indifferent to terror or worship
We are insects pinned beneath glass
Watching the ceiling of existence bend lower
With each shuddering breath of the firmament
Cities kneel; spires buckle under unseen hands
Rivers stall, thickening to pitch
The moon turns its face as though ashamed
Children of ash wander the streets
Tracing sigils in the soot that once was home
Every dream convulses
Nightmares bleed into the morning
Sleep offers no exile
The air itself grows fangs of frost
Gnawing at the edges of memory
I lift my eyes and see nothing
And yet that nothing sees me
Filling my lungs with the breath of extinction
Its stare is the absence of stars
Its shadow, the measure of eternity
For one crystalline instant
The world inhales in unison
In that fragile hush
Each soul feels a palm pressed gently to its chest
Not in comfort
But as a reminder of ownership
Bones remember the grip long after the touch withdraws
This insurmountable evil
Hung above all people
Outlasts ruin, devotion, and time
Hope wicks away like oil to flame
Resolving splinters into fine black snow
Still we raise trembling hands, not to fend it off
But to feel its magnitude
And know, at last
The scale of our smallness
Above us
Within us
